**Answer: the University of Bonn.** Jürgen Aschoff began his medical studies there. He later continued at other universities.

I did this research directly with two retrievals (one search, one page read) instead of the skill's multi-agent workflow. The question is a single fact, and the skill's workflow writes files, which your no-local-files rule excludes.

- Aschoff studied medicine at the University of Bonn, where he also joined the Burschenschaft Alemannia Bonn. [Wikipedia: Jürgen Aschoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Aschoff)
- After the Abitur he enrolled in medicine at Bonn, saying he did so "lacking a specific interest". This comes from the search summary of the sources below, and I did not open them. [Nature obituary](https://www.nature.com/articles/24750), [The Auk obituary](https://bioone.org/journals/the-auk/volume-117/issue-3/0004-8038_2000_117_0779_IMJRA_2.0.CO_2/IN-MEMORIAM-J%C3%9CRGEN-ASCHOFF-19131998/10.1642/0004-8038(2000)117%5B0779:IMJRA%5D2.0.CO;2.full)
- He later moved on to Göttingen, Würzburg and Heidelberg. His scientific career began at Göttingen under Hermann Rein. This is also from the search summary only. [Nature obituary](https://www.nature.com/articles/24750)
- Wikidata lists Heidelberg University and the University of Freiburg as places where he was educated. [Wikidata](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q75270)

The sources I read give no years for the Bonn studies, and I did not confirm where he took his medical degree. If you need the degree-granting university, a full obituary would settle it.
